summary: Petition under sections 79(1)(c) and 79(1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 19(3) of the CERC (Indian Electricity Grid Code) (first amendment) Regulations, 2024 (seeking extension of time for infirm power injection); and Regulation 57 of The CERC (Indian Electricity Grid Code) Regulations, 2023 read with Regulation 65 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Conduct Of Business) Regulations,2023, seeking relaxation/extension of the time prescribed for filing the present Petition. **7.** Since Petitioner commissioned 8 out of the 12 WTGs for which FTC approvals were granted on 06.08.2025 and 07.08.2025. However, due to unavoidable and unforeseeable circumstances such as severe law and order issues, RoW issues, and unprecedented monsoon, 4 WTGs being WTG Nos. 18 (SPI-172), 19 (TXI-80), 23 (TXI-199) and 47 (TXI-209), yet remain to be energised even after the expiry of the original FTC approvals on 30.09.2025 and 25.11.2025, respectively. ## **11.** Despite WRLDC expressly accepting the Petitioner’s explanations and justifications **14.** Petition is being filed on 13.01.2026 after a delay of 38 days, and thus the Petitioner seeks condonation of the delay in filing the instant petition under the Commission’s power to relax. The Petitioner has at all times acted diligently and has undertaken continuous mitigation efforts. Despite the above constraints, the Petitioner has successfully commissioned the majority of the Project capacity, remobilised resources at the site, and is fully ready to energize the remaining WTGs and complete all precommissioning and commissioning activities within the extended period sought, i.e., 45 days. **16.** During the course of the hearing, learned counsel for the Petitioner reiterated the contents already submitted in the Petition. After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission admitted the Petition with direction to notice to Respondents. The Petitioner was directed to submit (i.) Detailed reasons for noncompletion of the trial run and commissioning of the part capacity after obtaining FTC approval for the same, and (ii) detailed information of capacity commissioned along with the date up to which infirm injection permission is required in the prescribed format. **17.** Petitioner, in compliance with RoP for hearing dated 21.01.2026, has made the following submission vide affidavit dated 03.02.2026: - (c) The 4 WTGs in question, despite the Petitioner’s best efforts, could not be energised in time owing to factors completely beyond the control of the Petitioner. The delay was thus not attributable to any lack of readiness or diligence on the part of the Petitioner. **18.** During the course of the hearing, learned counsel submitted that Petitioner has filed the compliance affidavit dated 3.2.2026 as directed by the Commission vide Record of Proceedings dated 21.1.2026 and also sought liberty to rectify certain typographical errors in the compliance affidavit. **20.** After hearing the learned counsel for the Petitioner and the representative of the Respondent, the Commission directed the Petitioner to file the rectification of typographical errors and reserved the matter for Order. **21.** Petitioner vide affidavit dated 17.02.2026 filed rectified table related to connectivity and commissioning details of project elements as under: **23.** Petitioner, has submitted WRLDC on 05.01.2026 has extended validity of FTC till 14.04.2026 for WTG-18 and WTG-19, and till 27.05.2026 for WTG-23 and WTG-47. Petitioner vide affidavit dated 03.02.2026 has submitted that it will require about 45 days from the CERC Order for completing commissioning activities of these WTGs, whereas in the main Petition, the commissioning plan submitted by the Petitioner, has sought 31 days from the CERC Order, which is as under: **24.** We have perused the submissions of the Petitioner and the information on record. ## **2) Whether the Petitioner can be granted an extension of time for the injection of infirm power?** _The Commission, for reasons to be recorded in writing, may relax any of the provisions of these regulations on its own motion or on an application made before it by an affected person to remove the hardship arising out of the operation of any of these regulations, applicable to a class of persons.”_ **26.** The Petitioner is seeking relaxation of the 38-day time limit as the instant Petition has been filed with a 17-day delay. For this relaxation, Petitioner is praying for the relaxation under Regulation 57 of the amended IEGC, 2024. Regulation 57 is reproduced as below: _The Commission, for reasons to be recorded in writing, may relax any of the provisions of these regulations on its own motion or on an application made before it by an affected person to remove the hardship arising out of the operation of any of these regulations, applicable to a class of persons.”_ Considering the submissions made by the Petitioner regarding the factors cited as being beyond its control, it is observed that the circumstances leading to the delay were outside the Petitioner’s reasonable control. This Commission therefore condones a delay in filing of the Petition. **28.** Petitioner has submitted the following reasons for non-completion of the trial run and commissioning activities related to the pending WTGs as under: **30.** As discussed above, we are of the opinion that a one-month plan for trial run and commissioning provided by the Petitioner is reasonable instead of 45 days (indicated by the petitioner, vide affidavit dated 03.02.2026), to complete all pending activities related to the impugned Wind Turbines. Therefore, we condone the delay in filing the Petition and under Regulation 19(3) of the Grid Code, allow the Petitioner an extension of the period for interchange of power, up to one month from the date of issuance of this Order.
